## Must fix before opening

### 1 · Tooltip trigger is not focusable — the network list is unreachable by keyboard · P1 · regression/a11y

**File:** `apps/web/src/components/safe-apps/SafeAppPreviewDrawer/index.tsx:100`

```tsx
<NetworksTooltipTrigger render={<span className="inline-flex origin-left scale-85" />}>
```

Base UI's `Tooltip.Trigger` renders a `<button>` by default. The `render` prop *replaces* that element, so the trigger becomes a plain `<span>` — not focusable, no role, not in the tab order. The tooltip opens on pointer hover only.

Before this change every network name was rendered as visible text. Now only three logos and `+N` are. So the information didn't move to a secondary affordance — it moved to an affordance a keyboard-only user cannot operate. A screen-reader user gets the three visible logos' `alt` text (`"{chainName} Logo"`, `ChainIndicator/index.tsx:66`) and the literal string `+2`; the remaining network names are not in the accessibility tree at all.

**The repo already solved this.** The nearest sibling — same `TooltipTrigger` + `NetworkLogosList` + `ChainIndicator` composition — does it correctly:

```tsx
// AccountItemChainBadge.tsx:22
<TooltipTrigger render={<span />} tabIndex={0} className="flex items-center">
```

The other precedent, `SpaceAddressBookTable.tsx:63`, keeps the default `<button>` and puts the span *inside* as a child. Both stay reachable. This change is the only one of the three that is not.

**Fix:** add `tabIndex={0}` to the trigger, matching `AccountItemChainBadge.tsx:22`. If the `+N` badge should also announce what it hides, give the cluster an `aria-label` listing the full set — but `tabIndex` alone clears the blocking defect.

## Worth a ticket

### 2 · Third verbatim copy of the network-cluster-with-tooltip pattern · P2 · DRY

**File:** `apps/web/src/components/safe-apps/SafeAppPreviewDrawer/index.tsx:99-110`

This block is a character-for-character copy of `SpaceAddressBookTable.tsx:62-77` (`renderChains`) — same `inline-flex origin-left scale-85` class string, same `showHasMore maxVisible={3}`, same `flex flex-col gap-1` tooltip body. `AccountItemChainBadge.tsx:18-35` is the same pattern a third time, differing only in that it wraps it in a named, prop-typed component.

The global standard is to extract on the third write, and this is the third. The concrete cost is already visible: finding 1 exists *because* the copy silently diverged from its source on the one attribute that mattered. A fourth copy will diverge somewhere else.

**Fix:** promote the pattern to one exported component — `AccountItemChainBadge`'s multi-chain branch is already 90% of it — and have all three sites call it. That also retires the `scale-85` transform in favour of `NetworkLogosList`'s purpose-built `imageSize` prop (`NetworkLogosList/index.tsx:15`), which `MultichainSafeRow.tsx:232` already uses as `imageSize={18}`.

### 3 · Tests mock away everything they claim to test · P2 · testing

**File:** `apps/web/src/components/safe-apps/SafeAppPreviewDrawer/index.test.tsx:7-21`

Both `NetworkLogosList` and `ChainIndicator` are replaced with stubs, so the suite verifies prop plumbing and nothing rendered. Applying the revert test — *which test fails if I break this?* — the answer for finding 1 is *none*. Removing the trigger's focusability, or its `render` prop entirely, leaves all six tests green.

Two concrete weaknesses inside that:

- **`index.test.tsx:71-76`** — `'passes every chain to the cluster so overflow collapses beyond the visible limit'` asserts only that `data-networks` splits into 5 entries. That is a strict subset of line 66's assertion in the previous test, and the overflow collapse it names lives entirely inside the mocked-out `NetworkLogosList`. The test is redundant and its name describes coverage that doesn't exist.
- **`index.test.tsx:78-88`** — the tooltip test runs with `KNOWN_CHAIN_IDS` deliberately equal to `safeAppMock.chainIds`, so it cannot detect the tooltip body rendering unfiltered chains. The filter is covered for the cluster (line 97) but not for the tooltip.

**Fix:** add one test that tabs to the trigger and asserts the tooltip opens — that is the test finding 1 needs. Then either delete the test at line 71 or rewrite it to assert `+N` overflow against the real `NetworkLogosList`.

## Ruled out

- **Security — n/a.** No auth, no user-controlled input, no new network calls. `chainIds` come from the CGW safe-apps API and are used as React children and `key`s, both escaped.
- **Performance — n/a.** `configs.some()` inside `.filter()` is O(n×m), but both are bounded and small (≤20 app chains × ~30 configs) and it runs once per drawer render. Not worth memoising.
- **Tooltip rendering behind the drawer.** I checked this because the tooltip portals out of the MUI `Drawer`. `--z-overlay: 1400` (`styles/shadcn.css:58`) sits above the Drawer's default 1200, and `usePortalContainer` falls back to `document.body` outside a provider (`ShadcnProvider.tsx:48-51`). Not a defect.
- **`scale-85` being a silent no-op.** Valid in Tailwind v4 (`tailwindcss: ^4.1.18`), which accepts arbitrary numeric scale values. It renders.
- **Redundant `showUnknown` guard.** The old code passed `showUnknown={false}`; the tooltip's `ChainIndicator` at `index.tsx:106` lets it default to `true`. Harmless today because `knownChainIds` is pre-filtered — the two guards agree. Only a trap if the filter is later removed, which is too speculative to file.
